articles.title: Atlanta Dream vs. Golden State Valkyries Game 7: How to watch the 2026 WNBA Finals, channel, where to stream and more
articles.summary: Here's where to watch Game 7 of the 2026 WNBA Finals.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream were not about to lose Game 6 of the 2026 WNBA Finals on their home turf. The Dream defeated the Golden State Valkyries on Thursday, 69-80, forcing the series to a tiebreaking Game 7 (the first-ever Game 7 in the WNBA Finals!). The series will head back to the Bay Area for the final championship game this Saturday night (Happy Halloween!) at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT on USA Network, or stream it live on Peacock.

Here's what you need to know about watching Saturday's Game 7 of the WNBA Finals.

How to watch the Atlanta Dream vs. Golden State Valkyries Game 7

Streaming: Peacock , YouTube TV and more

The Dream vs. Valkyries Game 7 of the WNBA Finals tips off Oct. 31 at 8 p.m. ET.

What channel is Dream vs. Valkyries Game 7 on?

Game 7 of the WNBA Finals will air on USA and streams on Peacock.

Where to watch the WNBA Finals without cable

You can tune in to NBC via live TV platforms like YouTube TV, DirecTV and Fubo. Every Finals game also streams live on Peacock.

Game 1: Oct. 17, 3:30 p.m. ET, NBC and Peacock

Game 2: Oct. 19, 8 p.m. ET, Peacock, USA Network

Game 3: Oct. 21, 8 p.m. ET, Peacock, USA Network

Game 4: Oct. 24, 1 p.m. ET, NBC and Peacock

Game 5: Oct. 26, 8 p.m. ET, Peacock, USA Network

Game 6: Oct. 29, 12:30 p.m. ET, Peacock, USA Network

Game 7: Oct. 31, 8 p.m. ET, Peacock, USA Network

articles.title: WNBA Finals Game 7 Sets Ticket Price Record As Game 6 Seats Plummet To Just $23
articles.summary: From a $23 Game 6 seat in Atlanta to a $396 Game 7 entry fee in San Francisco, the Dream-Valkyries Finals have produced a wild ticket market.
articles.body:
Same series. Same league. Wildly different price tags.

The cheapest seat for WNBA Finals Game 6 in Atlanta dropped to $23 on TickPick ahead of Thursday's 12:30 p.m. ET tip. The get-in price for Game 7 in San Francisco is $396 on that same site, which calls it the most expensive game in league history.

The Game 6 slide has a clear starting point. The game was moved to State Farm Arena, and the early start was meant to keep it from bleeding into the Atlanta Hawks' game later that day. For fans back in San Francisco, that meant a 9:30 a.m. PT tip. The Spun called 12:30 p.m. ET one of the more unusual tip times for a Finals series.

The TickPick price was $156 when the game was announced Monday, and just two days later it was $23, an 85% drop. Game 6 seats had fallen from more than $100 to under $30, and pitching the game as an easy excuse for a sick day.

" Tickets were going for $156 before the announcement and are now just $23… For a Game 6 Finals game, " the X user posted.

The Dream announced that State Farm Arena was already sold out , and Atlanta filled the place despite the 9:30 a.m. PT start. Angel Reese had scored just eight and seven points in Games 4 and 5, and the Dream lost both, so Atlanta arrived at Game 6 one loss from elimination with a lot to prove.

The Dream beat Golden State 80-69, behind 23 points and six rebounds from Allisha Gray and 14 rebounds from Angel Reese, to force the first Finals Game 7 in WNBA history. Golden State had won two straight, including a 64-55 grind in Game 5, so the Dream needed a statement, and they got it.

Why WNBA Finals Game 7 Tickets Cost So Much More Than Game 6

Game 7 tips off Saturday night at 8 p.m. ET at Chase Center on Halloween, in a game billed as Boohalla, and the secondary market has treated it like a heavyweight title fight.

On Thursday afternoon, the get-in prices are listed at $430 on Ticketmaster, $409 on StubHub, $376 on Vivid Seats, $370 on SeatGeek, and $365 on Gametime. TickPick sat at $396.

The better seats climb even faster, because many lower-bowl seats approached or topped $1,000 and courtside seats were listed in the thousands. One pair on SeatGeek was posted at $12,549 per ticket, and a pair on Ticketmaster asked $13,196 per seat.

The stakes explain a lot of that, since neither franchise has ever won a WNBA title and the Valkyries are only two seasons old. Golden State sold out every home game in its historic regular season, so a packed Saturday crowd is the safe bet, and sellers know it.

Put the two prices side by side, and the gap is hard to miss. A $23 seat in Atlanta against a $396 seat in San Francisco is a difference of $373, or roughly 17 times. That is not a perfect comparison. Game 6 was a weekday game that started around lunchtime, while Game 7 is a winner-take-all game on a Saturday night at a home arena known for sellouts.

Still, the Game 6 slide began right after the league confirmed the venue and the start time. Atlanta fans got a bargain bin, while Bay Area fans are getting a bidding war. Saturday's tip is primetime, and one team will finally have its first championship. At these prices, the market already knows what that moment is worth.

articles.title: WNBA Finals: Dream, Valkyries delivering on the promise of what a 7-game series offers
articles.summary: This tense, historic matchup is what the WNBA had in mind when the league began the Finals format last season.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The WNBA can finally use the best two words in sports: Game 7.

For the first time in the league's 30-year history, the championship will be decided at the end of a full seven-game series when the No. 2 Golden State Valkyries and No. 4 Atlanta Dream take the Chase Center court on Saturday (8 p.m. ET, USA Network). The Valkyries and Dream are building anticipation, even when the basketball hasn't been all that great for those who want to see the scorebug budge more than every few minutes.

It's a gift the league will heartily embrace on the heels of yet another week of bungling its own product — and after a dud of a Finals in its first attempt at the format last season. In hindsight, expecting an extended series between the Las Vegas Aces and Phoenix Mercury a year ago, when the league changed the format from best-of-five, was foolish. The Aces and WNBA can be quite the thorn in each other's side. Las Vegas won its third title in four years with an uneventful sweep.

There is none of that here, proving the league's brass correct that the game was ready for the big time.

Yet the WNBA remains mired in oddities, to put it kindly. That a potential elimination Game 6 tipped at 12:30 p.m. ET on a Thursday was proof enough. The playoff standings are based on the top eight, without regard to conferences. It wasn't until four years ago that the league ditched the single-elimination first and second-round bracket that sent the top two teams directly to the semifinals. Even the Finals previously stood as a standalone game that later changed to best-of-three in 1998 and best-of-five in 2005.

Crowning a champion within five games didn't set the league apart. It kept it away.

"This will give our fans a championship series that they are accustomed to seeing in other sports," WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert said when she announced the change ahead of Game 1 of the 2024 WNBA Finals.

The "real" professional sports all play seven-games series. The NBA began with it in 1947 when the Basketball Association of America governed the league. The NHL's Stanley Cup Finals adopted it in 1939, having used it once prior in 1919 when it was the NHL versus the Pacific Coast Hockey Association in the final. MLB started the format, initiating it in 1905 and remaining unchanged with the exception of three seasons from 1919-21.

Those years baseball expanded, not contracted, to best-of-nine. The reason was simple: gate receipts. You didn't think WNBA brass did this simply for funsies, did you? More games is more money in every stakeholder's pocket. There's a lot of green to go around these days. Every game has been a sellout, no matter the tip time or change of schedule.

To expand to seven any earlier was a leap too far for the fledgling WNBA. It still flew commercial until 2024, making for long and grueling travel days. Even with charter flights, the length of the series coupled with five-hour cross-country flights is taking a toll .

It's unlikely ESPN, the WNBA's TV partner since 2003, was pushing for more in the 2010s. It hid the playoffs on deeper channels, leaning instead into more lucrative and enticing deals with the MLB playoffs, NFL's "Monday Night Football," college football and NBA. It would not be surprising if cornhole and laser tag usurped the WNBA in a past era.

As a measuring stick of low points, the 2014 Finals — featuring Diana Taurasi's Mercury and Elena Della Donne's Sky — averaged 659,000 viewers, up 91% from the prior year's Lynx/Dream series (345,000) and 38% above the 2012 Fever/Lynx (477,000). And those were celebratory marks as the most-watched since at least 2006.

My how far the league has come. The 2025 Finals averaged 1.5 million despite the sweep, ranking as the second-most-watched W Finals on ESPN's networks. A record 1.9 million tuned in for Game 1 of what was expected to be an even series amid talks of growing parity and two surprising contenders.

The broadcaster's record is 2024, when 1.6 million on average tuned in for the series between New York and Minnesota that could have used the extended format. The Lynx stole Game 1, forced a Game 5, and took the Liberty to overtime before New York escaped to win its first championship in franchise history. As the series chugged along, the wisecracks rose that Engelbert would appear out of thin air midgame to announce an early format change on a whim. Everyone wanted the testy, tight series to burn another two games.

This now is what the league's leaders envisioned then. The Dream and Valkyries answered each other the last two weeks. They split the two-game stretches in San Francisco and Atlanta, setting up a 1-1-1 best-of-three. Each held home court in championship-worthy environments that once held only in dreams.

They forced the 14th winner-take-all game in league Finals history. The home team has won 11 of those. Game by game, viewership numbers are rising. The Valkyries' Game 5 win averaged 1.4 million, the second-most-watched Game 5 ever — significant since every other previous one was winner-take-all.

Time and again, the product proves it is worth a position on the major sports carousel. In a historic year that began with a revenue-sharing collective bargaining agreement, it will end with another watermark financial boon. A first-time WNBA champion will be crowned no matter the winner at the final buzzer of the first Game 7.

The league is finally stacking good history now.

articles.title: New York Knicks vs. Philadelphia 76ers Live NBA Updates, Scores and Highlights
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers opened up the NBA Cup on Friday night with their second straight win over the New York Knicks, leaving Xfinity Mobile Arena with the 98-93 victory.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers opened up the NBA Cup on Friday night with their second straight win over the New York Knicks, leaving Xfinity Mobile Arena with the 98-93 victory.

With Jaylen Brown sidelined by a left knee injury, Philly's other stars came out to play. LeBron James turned in his first 20-point game with the Sixers, including the game-sealing bucket on an offensive rebound. He also racked up nine rebounds and eight assists.

Tyrese Maxey was brilliant through and through. He pumped out 27 points and four assists on 10-of-19 shooting. Anfernee Simons pitched in 21 points on 7-of-11 shooting off the bench. VJ Edgecombe scored 13 points and grabbed eight boards while hustling on defense. Joel Embiid only had 10 points, but he was the engine powering the offense as a facilitator early. He finished with seven assists.

The Knicks continue to struggle from beyond the arc and with their overall offensive process. Jalen Brunson (24 points, six assists) and Karl-Anthony Towns (22 points, 12 rebounds) led the way for them. They are now 2-4 on the season.

Scroll below for all the best highlights, analysis, postgame comments and takeaways from Friday's NBA Cup showdown.

Tyrese Maxey being the best player in a game that featured LeBron James, Joel Embiid, Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns has become the new norm. No wonder why LeBron likes (loves?) him so much.

Karl-Anthony Towns Weighs in on Knicks' Struggles

"Lightning doesn't strike twice" is a bar.

Whether that's supposed to comfort Knicks fans is...debatable.

"I don't think about it," LeBron said of his longevity.

That's perfectly fine, Mr. James. We are constantly thinking about it, and posting about it, on your behalf.

Jalen Brunson Says What All Knicks Fans are Thinking

Both of the Knicks' wins this season have notably come after trailing by double-digits. They fell behind by 10 points against the (Jalen Duren-less) Detroit Pistons. And then they railed by as many as 19 against the Chicago Bulls.

New York's biggest deficit against Philly was 14 points. While it's cool the Knicks have shown they can climb out of big holes over and over again, they're not going to avoid burnout if they need to keep expending a ton of energy to come back from behind.

That Next Sixers Injury Report is Going to be Something

Saturday marks Philly's second back-to-back of the season. We already know LeBron and Embiid won't be playing both ends. Jaylen Brown's left knee injury doesn't sound like a one-night-off thing. Dean Wade wasn't healthy to start the year and could require maintenance.

Philly may need to start four guards in Charlotte. I'm kind of here for it.

LeBron is in Love with Tyrese Maxey's...Punctuality

There is perhaps nothing more 41-years-old than using punctuality as an analog for future greatness.

Can't wait to see whether LeBron says the same about Joel.

LeBron Throws More Praise Tyrese Maxey's Way

Is "legendary status" something that can be passed down? Does Tyrese Maxey even need LeBron's help?

Why hasn't anybody offered to pass any of their legendary qualities down to me?

Karl-Anthony Towns is Wearing a Wrap on His Wrist

Towns was questionable entering tonight's game with a left wrist injury, so this will be something to track moving forward.

Fortunately for the Knicks, this isn't his shooting hand. The team also doesn't play again until Monday, which gives Towns an opportunity to rest it.

At least Jalen Brunson didn't lose the game and his sense of humor.

For those wondering, Brunson is 30 and Josh Hart is 31.

Nick Nurse is right. This was LeBron's best game as a Sixer.

Josh Hart Offers Perspective on the Knicks' Slow Start

Is this "someone's out of shape" shade? Or just an acknowledgement the Knicks are working off not only a championship, consecutive deep playoff runs to the conference finals and beyond?

Either way, good luck getting fans to accept that it's going to take time. Some will understand. But this team has billed itself as being above the championship fatigue.

LeBron's Handshakes with his Teammates Stop for Nothing and No One

Mike Brown Explains What's Wrong with the Knicks' Defense

Too long, didn't watch version: The Knicks aren't doing a good job containing the ball, executing traps or communicating.

New York's ball-containment was especially problematic in this one. Tyrese Maxey is fast, but there's zero excuse for letting the Sixers as a team shoot 15-of-19 (78.9 percent) at the rim.

On second thought, after watching him perfectly hit The Silencer, get this kid ALL the candy.

Nick Nurse Comments on LeBron's Performance

Let's good ahead and rank all of LeBron's Sixers performance so far:

This order is beyond reproach and will not be changed.

The iso bit feels aimed at OG Anunoby. It could also be directed towards Jalen Brunson, but he's supposed to have carte blanche.

The home-run comment could apply to Karl-Anthony Towns. He's too often overcomplicating his playmaking responsibilities, seemingly waiting for the highlight pass rather than looking to strictly move the ball or drive-and-kick.

No Jaylen Brown? No problem. Apparently.

You have to hand it to the Sixers. LeBron and Maxey were steadying presences all night, and they got pockets of excellence from Embiid, Simons and Edgecombe at different points in the game.

This team isn't perfect, but it's sure tough to beat.

LeBron continues to wear many different hats for the Sixers this season. Philly closed this one out following a pair of made free throws by Tyrese Maxey.

LeBron Just About Wraps It Up for the Sixers

Brilliant night from LeBron. But credit Tyrese Maxey for getting around the Knicks' defense, breaking the paint and causing the chaos that freed up James for the offensive rebound.

Jalen Brunson sank 1-of-2 free throws. Philly is up three with 31.7 seconds remaining.

If this call isn't overturned, Jalen Brunson officially has one of the best whistles of all time.

(For what it's worth, Brunson appears to be fine.)

LeBron James made a fadeaway jumper. The Knicks followed that up with a missed Jalen Brunson jumper. And then, VJ Edgecombe did this.

Score: Sixers 94, Knicks 90 | 30.8 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter

Some absurd shot-making is happening down the stretch here.

Karl-Anthony Hits a Clutch 3 from Another Area Code

This KAT shot is crazy. Even crazier? Him low-fiving Jalen Brunson so hard that JB's surgically repaired wrist appears to be in pain.

After not playing at all through the first three quarters, Jordan Clarkson started the fourth and has helped keep the Knicks afloat with his defensive hustle, an and-1 opportunity out of a drive, and a key offensive rebound he converted for a bucket.

Score: Sixers 87, Knicks 82 | 6:26 remaining in the fourth quarter

If you search "What is a microwave scorer?" it'll bring you to a copy of Anfernee Simons' birth certificate.

Anfernee Simons came off the bench in the third and promptly torched the Knicks for nine points of 4-of-5 shooting. He is now up to 16 points on the evening—in under 20 minutes of action.

New York's defense inexplicably lost track of him or unnecessarily went under on a screen against him at least twice. But his perimeter shot-making is a second-unit cheat code. Especially for the bargain price of $6 million.

Sixers 77, Knicks 68 | End of the third quarter

LeBron with the Chasedown Goaltend, Er, I Mean Block

Goaltending rules are apparently different if you're over the age of 40.

Score: Sixers 72, Knicks 60 | 2:30 remaining in the third quarter

The year is 2056. A 71-year-old LeBron James is still making stupid-awesome crosscourt passes.

Even his transition looks are difficult. Jeez.

Don't stop me if you're heard this one before. You have.

Jalen Brunson is both making shots and an effort to get deeper into the paint. Mikal Bridges has disrupted two Tyrese Maxey possessions in just a couple of minutes. Led by seven Brunson points, the Knicks are on a 10-1 run.

Score: Sixers 59, Knicks 54 | 7:20 remaining in the third quarter

Don't sleep on that LeBron pass for Maxey's second bucket, by the way. One of the sicker kick-outs that you'll see from anyone.

Maxey has opened the third quarter on his own personal 5-0 run and is up to 23 points on the evening. Knicks head coach Mike Brown wasted little time calling a timeout as Philly expands the lead to 14.

Score: Sixers 58, Knicks 44 | 10:19 remaining in the third quarter

I would say Embiid's going to feel that one tomorrow, but he's feeling it right now.

The Sixers Take a 9-Point Lead into the Locker Room

Tyrese Maxey is putting on another show at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Between his and LeBron's scoring and Embiid's facilitation, the offense has verged on unstoppable.

Philly's defense is just as impressive. The Knicks have missed a few perimeter bunnies, but the Sixers are cutting off their dribble penetration and keeping them out of transition. Dean Wade has been incredible on the less-glamorous end, too.

Karl-Anthony Towns leads the way for New York with nine points. Deuce McBride's seven points are the Knicks' only bench production. Given their inability to get to the rim (5-of-8), low free-throw profile (four attempts) and poor three-point shooting (7-of-22), they're lucky to only be down nine.

LeBron's scoring aggression has waxed and waned to start the season. With Jaylen Brown out, he appears more bent on looking for his own shot. He has 12 points on nine field-goal attempts in the first half.

The Sixers' Offense has Found Its Groove

Philly ranked 29th in points scored per possession entering Friday. That's definitely changing after tonight.

The Sixers' swing game and overall ball movement is popping. Joel Embiid is wearing his facilitator hat, which has helped preserve flow. LeBron has now hit a couple jumpers.

Tyrese Maxey has punctured the Knicks' interior defense on multiple occasions. VJ Edgecombe is 5-of-5 inside the arc. The Sixers' are running when they're not in the half-court. It's a sight to behold.

Score: Sixers 46, Knicks 38 | 2:30 remaining in the second quarter

The Knicks' Offense is in the Mud Right Now

New York is heavily featuring Anunoby on-ball, and it's resulted in a lot of possessions to nowhere. Put another way:

The Knicks' struggles aren't on Anunoby alone. They're now up to seven turnovers. They can't hit threes. And the Sixers have kept them out of transition.

Score: Sixers 37, Knicks 26 | 7:10 remaining in the second quarter

OG will probably think twice before going with the finger roll over the dunk next time.

Philly Leads by 8 Points at the End of the First Quarter

Both the Sixers (3-of-9) and Knicks (3-of-11) are struggling to find their touch from deep. New York has yet to attempt a free throw. Philly has yet to grab an offensive rebound.

Turnovers are a swing factor thus far. The Knicks committed four in the opening frame while the Sixers had none. Philly also got a ton of playmaking from Embiid (three assists).

Score: Sixers 29, Knicks 21 | End of the first quarter

This is an example of the defensive activity from Embiid I just referenced. Just an excellent job by him sliding into the gap on Jalen Brunson's drive without overcommitting.

The 6'4" VJ Edgecombe burying a step-back jumper over the seven-foot Karl-Anthony Towns is a totally normal thing for a sophomore to do. Nothing to see here.

Philly has opened a double-digit lead. The Knicks are once again getting derailed by ball pressure, and Joel Embiid was active on the defensive end before taking a seat.

Score: Sixers 29, Knicks 19 | 46.4 seconds remaining in the first quarter

You love to see it. Unless you're a Knicks fan.

Jalen Brunson Drills One in Tyrese Maxey's Face

Look at the way Jalen Brunson stares down Tyrese Maxey. This is just good ol' fashion supervillain stuff from the reigning Finals MVP.

Score: Sixers 18, Knicks 11 | 4:47 remaining in the first quarter

LeBron entered the game shooting 23.1 percent from beyond the arc on the season. His mid-range touch hasn't been much better. Let's see if hitting an early triple gets him going from the perimeter.

All it took was the Sixers landing LeBron James and Jaylen Brown over the same offseason to weed out stray Knicks fans in these Philly-New York clashes. Reasonable enough.

Anyway, the Sixers hold an early lead, thanks largely to nifty shot-making from LeBron and Tyrese Maxey.

Score: Sixers 14, Knicks 11 | 6:05 remaining in the first quarter

The Sixers will no doubt futz and fiddle with these head-to-heads as the game goes on. During the opening night tilt, Nick Nurse eventually put LeBron James on Karl-Anthony Towns so Joel Embiid could roam.

Score: Sixers 12, Knicks 9 | 7:35 remaining in the first quarter

LeBron is Enjoying His Time with the 76ers

Do we think it's the free helicopter rides or the opportunity to play with Tyrese Maxey?

Mike Brown Addresses Surge of NBA Injuries

Why would he even put this out there?!? Somebody sage the Knicks' locker room and team plane and then jet down to Madison Square Garden and repeat the process.

Nick Nurse Offers High Praise for Tyrese Maxey

On a team so laden with big names, most of whom prefer to operate on-ball, many wondered whether Tyrese Maxey might get lost in Philly's saturated hierarchy.

Like he has on numerous other versions of the Sixers, though, he continues to prove his stardom will scale to any situation. And if there was ever any doubt over who'd be this team's best player, he's put that to bed, too.

The Sixers' Starters Have Yet to Play Together

As expected, Dean Wade is sliding into Philly's starting five alongside Tyrese Maxey, LeBron James, VJ Edgecombe and Joel Embiid. While that's the right call relative to defensive volume the Sixers must paper over without Brown, this particular fivesome has yet to log a single minute together.

The biggest question: Does this group have enough shooting? Brown isn't the most deadeye sniper, but he's shooting well from deep to start the season. Generally speaking, he's also a more willing three-point taker than Wade.

Inserting Anfernee Simons instead was almost assuredly a non-starter. But with LeBron shooting 25 percent on looks away from the rim , the offensive output of this quintet is worth monitoring.

Karl-Anthony Towns is a GO for the Knicks

With the exception of Jose Alvarado (ankle), the Knicks will have their full cast of characters available to open the NBA Cup.

As far as Karl-Anthony Towns' wrist injury goes, Knicks fans can breathe a sigh of relief. Well that, or they should be terrified he's pushing the bill too hard in the good name of defending New York's NBA Cup title.

"Not able to go through shootaround" doesn't sound great knowing how light those tend to be. Here's hoping this is the Sixers operating with an overabundance of caution.

In the meantime, Dean Wade is expected to get the start in Jaylen Brown's place.

articles.title: Los Angeles Lakers vs. Golden State Warriors Live NBA Updates, Scores and Highlights
articles.summary: The round two tussle between Yaxel Lendeborg and Luka Dončić never materialized. The basketball gods tossed the towel on that one at some point during a 21-point first quarter for Dončić (a scoreless frame for Lendeborg).
articles.body:
The round two tussle between Yaxel Lendeborg and Luka Dončić never materialized. The basketball gods tossed the towel on that one at some point during a 21-point first quarter for Dončić (a scoreless frame for Lendeborg).

Unfortunately for Dončić, this wasn't a one-on-one battle with the fearless freshman. He and the Los Angeles Lakers were tussling with the entirety of the Golden State Warriors to open NBA Cup play, and the Warriors took this tilt in signature strength-in-numbers style.

While Stephen Curry supplied the most powerful punch with 31 points and eight three-pointers, it took a village to pull off this 112-95 win. And the village came through. Brandin Podziemski had 21 points, Draymond Green masterminded the defense and the bench built a colossal 50-7 advantage. The Warriors assisted on 31 of their 38 field goals and recovered from a sloppy start to win the turnover margin 15-20.

Dončić had 37 points, and Austin Reaves added 21 points, but they also had 11 turnovers and 15 missed threes between them. And they had zero offensive consistency from the players around them, with L.A. shooting a collective 33-of-82 overall (40.2 percent) and 11-of-39 from three (28.2 percent).

It was a wild win for the Warriors and a frustrating loss for the Lakers, and we were around to real-time document all of it.

Two elite scorers, two elite offensive showmen, and they left it all out on the court.

Warriors' Vets Coaching Up Yaxel Lendeborg

It was a rough night for the rookie—and a poorly timed one given how much attention was focused on him (and, it's worth noting, directed there by him)—but the Warriors know they'll need him to deliver.

So, much like Jimmy Butler did earlier in the contest, Draymond Green offered some words of wisdom afterward.

The Lakers looked lost once Luka took a breather in the second quarter, and they never found their way back. They can't play Dončić all 48 minutes and shouldn't need to given what they've invested in Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler, but they looked totally helpless without him. They won his 37 minutes by nine points—in a 17-point loss.

What a comeback. What a team effort. And what an absurd showing from Stephen Curry. The Lakers never could get Luka back in a groove after his 21-point opening quarter, nor find consistent scoring help around him.

There are fewer than three minutes left in regulation, and L.A.'s bench has five points. Five . Luka had a huge first quarter, but since it's been a few flashes from him and Austin Reaves, and then a lot of empty possessions.

Score: Warriors 105, Lakers 91 | 2:45 remaining in the fourth quarter

Steph (not Yaxel) vs. Luka has been worth the price of admission. They have 68 points and 14 three-pointers between them, and their highlight reels for endless.

But Golden State's support guards, namely Brandin Podziemski and De'Anthony Melton, are the reason why the Warriors are a strong finish away from a big win.

Score: Warriors 104, Lakers 91 | 3:11 remaining in the fourth quarter

I'm starting to think Dončić may not be a Steph stopper.

History's greatest shooter is a historic offensive force.

Curry Climbing the All-Time Scoring Ladder

With a three-point splash—fittingly assisted by Draymond Green—Stephen Curry jumped in front of Hall of Famer Dominique Wilkins for the 18th spot on the career scoring leaderboard. What a player, what a career.

Score: Warriors 96, Lakers 80 | 8:02 remaining in the fourth quarter

Dončić clearly has crushed this matchup, but Lendeborg did put a promising sequence on tape at least.

With a no-show from new second option, Yaxel Lendeborg, Golden State has needed someone else to step up. It has found a lot of someones on the bench, but Brandin Podziemski started coming alive in the third quarter and is making momentum-building plays on both ends.

Score: Warriors 90, Lakers 80 | 9:38 remaining in the fourth quarter

And E-40's reaction. Does anyone even remember the first quarter anymore?

Luka could do no wrong in the first, and Curry had a highlight make for the ages, but Golden State's second unit (and L.A.'s lack thereof) has emerged as the biggest factor in this contest.

The Lakers had a chance to bury the Lakers early (and virtually did with a 38-15 first quarter), but they never did. And as if saluting all of the zombies out there this Halloween weekend, the Warriors have risen from the dead and then some.

Score: Warriors 85, Lakers 80 | End of the third quarter

Save for Steph doing Steph things, it's been a mostly quiet night for the Warriors' starters. But their reserves are clobbering their counterparts, helping Golden State go on momentum-building runs in the second and third quarter now.

Score: Warriors 84, Lakers 80 | 0:21 remaining in the third quarter

This happened right after Dončić got dropped. Shot-makers are shot-making tonight. What a game.

Score: Lakers 78, Warriors 78 | 1:48 remaining in the third quarter

Score: Lakers 74, Warriors 70 | 3:35 remaining in the third quarter

Luka defending Steph in space just isn't a fair fight. Ankles!

Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg is going through it, but he has some pretty great veterans to lean on.

After a red-alert start this half, Golden State sits everyone not named Stephen Curry or Draymond Green. The game is still well within reach, but an out-of-hand quarter could change that in a hurry.

Score: Lakers 69, Warriors 60 | 6:34 remaining in the third quarter

Is Steph Curry sticking up for his rookie here? Or just roasting a favorable matchup?

The Lakers used Luka magic to build a huge advantage in the first quarter, then struggled to get anything going without him in the second. Their 13-4 start to the third frame, though, is mostly a credit to "the others." Austin Reaves and Jake LaRavia netted 11 of those points.

Score: Lakers 66, Warriors 57 | 7:27 remaining in the third quarter

Golden State going with a bigger group to start this half. And, perhaps to the chagrin of those tuning in to catch Luka v. Lendeborg, using Draymond Green to defend Dončić instead.

Score: Lakers 59, Warriors 53 | 10:16 remaining in the third quarter

A Sequence So Nice It's Worth Seeing Twice

Steph's gravity is just a permanent source of clean looks for his teammates. And he knows how to leverage it with on-point deliveries like this.

It was a very quiet first half for Yaxel Lendeborg (two points, one shot, five turnovers, three fouls), but at least he and all of us know how E-40 pronounces his name now.

The Lakers should not have looked as lost as they did without Luka. The offense was entrusted to Austin Reaves—a max-contract player with near-star (or All-Star) numbers so far—and he just couldn't deliver. He had 10 first-half points on 10 first-half shots and managed just four assists against six turnovers.

Rapid second quarter summary: Golden State stopped turning it over and started making shots, and L.A. stopped playing Luka Dončić. The Lakers won Luka's 19 minutes by 12 points, which means they lost the five he didn't play by that margin.

Podz Put the Finishing Touch on the First Half

Non-Steph starter scoring has been hard to find for Golden State tonight—two points for Yaxel Lendeborg ( on one shot?! ), none for Draymond Green or Gui Santos—but this timely triple from Brandin Podziemski knotted up a game that felt like it got away in the first quarter.

Warriors reserves have 30 points; Lakers reserves have three. Golden State completely flipped this script, mirroring L.A.'s 38-15 edge in the first quarter with an identical 38-15 advantage of its own in the second. We. Are. Tied.

Score: Lakers 53, Warriors 53 | End of second quarter

Golden State is officially grooving, and we absolutely have a game again.

Score: Lakers 53, Warriors 50 | 0:53 remaining in the second quarter

OK, One More Note on That First-Frame Flurry from Luka

The Lakers wobbled quite a bit when Dončić sat, but he gave them such a huge cushion early, they're still holding onto a double-digit lead.

Score: Lakers 51, Warriors 37 | 4:03 remaining in the second quarter

The Warriors are clearly compromised for size, so they'll welcome this little energy lift from Charles Bassey.

A brilliant block by Charles Bassey and a loud finish to get Yaxel Lendeborg on the scoreboard.

A Surprise Undercard to Luka v. Lendeborg?

Things have gotten chippy, but this wasn't the Dončić vs. Lendeborg bout folks have been waiting to see.

Hopefully getting video of this soon, but this sequence proved Golden State has some paint presence of its own. L.A. continuing to let this lead dwindle without Dončić.

Score: Lakers 44, Warriors 33 | 6:40 remaining in the second quarter

Georges Niang has given Golden State a spark tonight, but this block by Walker Kessler was purely electric.

Melton's attacks and a big Steph splash have the Warriors cooking to start this quarter. Lakers might need to summon Dončić soon.

Warriors Will Take Offense Wherever They Can Get It

Golden State starters not named Stephen Curry have two points on seven shots. Warriors not named Curry, Georges Niang or De'Anthony Melton have three total points. Still, credit those last two in particular for providing enough timely scores to keep this from getting totally out of hand.

While the Warriors are working to make a push with Dončić on the sideline, let's just keep marveling at the damage he did before taking a breather.

Score: Lakers 40, Warriors 28 | 9:30 remaining in the second quarter

As incredible as Dončić looked in the first quarter, the Warriors were equally rough. Golden State's starters have eight points on 11 shots.

Did, uh, Yaxel Lendeborg just set up Luka Dončić for a career-high kind of night? It's obviously early, considering he's had a 73-piece before, but he is on pace after a blistering first quarter.

Lendeborg, on the other hand, has three turnovers, two fouls and zero points, assists, steals or blocks.

It's a true Halloween Eve nightmare for the Warriors. They're getting trounced, their prized rookie, Lendeborg, is getting pummeled: no shots, no assists, no seals, no blocks, three turnovers and a minus-21 in eight minutes. Dončić, meanwhile, appears in a dream state.

Score: Lakers 35, Warriors 15 | 1:07 remaining in the first quarter

Hey, It Hasn't Been a Total Loss for Warriors Fans

Pretty brutal stuff all around for the Warriors. Make it nine turnovers and five field goals for Golden State. Yikes.

Score: Lakers 34, Warriors 15 | 1:23 remaining in the first quarter

I mean, a lot of them wind up "those nights," but Dončić looks totally unbothered by any defender around him. He has 14 points, four assists, two steals and a block in nine minutes of work.

Look, Luka can work his magic against anyone, but he seems a little extra revved for this one. Lendeborg and the Warriors better find a counter-punch pretty soon, or this could be over early.

Score: Lakers 28, Warriors 14 | 3:01 remaining in the first quarter

Luka Started His Night With a 3 Over Lendeborg

The Lakers are getting the better of the Warriors, and Dončić is making it obvious he heard every one of Lendeborg's sound bites.

It's been a very disjointed start for the Dubs offense, which has more turnovers (six) than assists (five) and a brutal connection rate on twos (1-of-6). But any time Stephen Curry shreds a night, it gets you a real "Anything is possible!" vibe.

Score: Lakers 25, Warriors 14 | 4:38 remaining in the first quarter

Objectively speaking, the Lakers overpaid for Walker Kessler this summer. But you can see why they—and seemingly Luka—deemed him a necessity.

Dončić can make the trash talk pretty simple so far: Scoreboard!

Score: Lakers 19, Warriors 11 | 7:07 remaining in the first quarter

For all of the attention on Lendeborg's ability to contain Luka, it's still not clear how Golden State plans to handle Kessler. He's picking up right where he left off with a 2-of-2 start, finishing both a soft jumper and a spoon-fed chance created by Dončić.

A lot of makes for the Lakers, a lot of sloppy giveaways for the Warriors.

Score: Lakers 12, Warriors 2 | 9:42 remaining in the first quarter

When the Warriors aren't running offense for Stephen Curry, they're finding it for their freshman. What an absurd acceleration up the pecking order.

The way tonight is going, it seems like folks are bringing their best for the start of NBA Cup play.

Curry is coming into this contest fresh off a 44-point, six-triple outburst. He went a perfect 16-of-16 from the line in that one.

Oh, and in the game before that, he didn't miss a shot from anywhere—8-of-8 from the field, 3-of-3 from range and 5-of-5 at the stripe. History's greatest shooter is very much feeling it.

Jake LaRavia Gets Second Straight Start for the Lakers

Just like Wednesday night (a 16-point win over the Los Angeles Clippers), the Lakers are plugging LaRavia into the starting spot vacated by the injured Ziaire Williams. That could be an offensive upgrade, though it doesn't automatically look that way with how Williams has shot it this season (46.7 percent).

Defensively, though, the Lakers use some athleticism and versatility.

The Warriors have used this lineup, which features only one player standing above 6'7" (the 6'9" Lendeborg), once this season. And it was their best performance by far—a 20-point takedown of Nikola Jokić and the Denver Nuggets.

It still feels a little worrisome given how much trouble Golden State had with Walker Kessler in the opener, but if this lineup can handle Jokić (19 points on 18 shots in that game), maybe it's ready for a second crack at this test.

Whatever Happens Tonight (and in the Future), Expect To Hear Yaxel Lendeborg's Thoughts on It

Lendeborg's unfiltered thoughts have upped the early entertainment factor of this season's start. And it sounds like they'll be around for a while now.

As they should be. Mostly. Look, coaches probably aren't huge fans of their players providing bulletin-board material for opponents, but these are professionals. They don't need someone else to set their edge. Besides, who uses bulletin boards anymore?

L.A. had no problem corralling Golden State's offense on opening night, but the Warriors are coming in hot after hanging 119-plus points on their past three opponents.

This could be a different kind of defensive challenge, and L.A. will have to tackle it minues one of its best defenders. That'll be two consecutive absences now for Ziaire Williams.

Think the Warriors know their rookie just might have a target on his back tonight? More likely they're preparing him as best they can for the defensive challenge of containing the current (and reigning) scoring leader and all of his on-ball trickery.

Yaxel Lendeborg Is Feeling the Halloween Spirit

What an entrance for the Warriors rookie tonight. A not-so-subtle message to Luke and friends? Almost certainly, yes. A strong play to be crowned king of the (one-man?) costume contest? An even more emphatic, Yes!

articles.title: UConn coach Dan Hurley agrees to contract extension through 2032
articles.summary: Dan Hurley does not appear to be planning to leave UConn anytime soon.
articles.body:
Dan Hurley does not appear to be planning to leave UConn anytime soon.

The UConn men's basketball coach has agreed to a new six-year contract that will keep him in Storrs through 2032, the school announced Friday . Hurley previously had four years remaining on the six-year, $50 million contract he signed in 2024 , so this is effectively a two-year extension.

According to the Associated Press , the new deal keeps Hurley's salary around $8 million, keeping him among the highest-paid coaches in college basketball. Kansas' Bill Self currently leads the group at $8.9 million .

It's little surprise that Hurley commands such pay, as it's hard to argue he hasn't been the most successful coach in the sport over the past five years. The Huskies won back-to-back titles in 2022-23 and 2023-24, and made a return trip to the national championship game earlier this year before losing to a historically talented Michigan team.

Hurley did meet with the Los Angeles Lakers about their open coaching job after winning that second title, but ultimately turned down a six-year, $70 million offer . Los Angeles went on to hire JJ Redick.

A statement from UConn athletic director David Benedict, via UConn's announcement:

"Dan has proven to be the very best coach in men's college basketball, and we're thrilled to keep him home at UConn for the next six years. His teams embody everything that UConn is about; resilience, competitive excellence and the pursuit of championships. In this chaotic era of college sports, it has never been more important to maintain continuity as we strive to compete at the highest level in everything we do."

This season's squad ranks fourth in the preseason AP Poll. UConn will open the season against Gardner-Webb on Monday.

articles.title: LeBron James Talks 76ers Adjustment After Lakers Career, Says He'll 'Get Better' as Season Continues
articles.summary: LeBron James doesn't feel he has yet hit his peak with the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
LeBron James doesn't feel he has yet hit his peak with the Philadelphia 76ers.

"I'm still adjusting. Eight years in LA... I am adjusting, still," James told NBA on Prime's Steve Nash ahead Friday night's NBA Cup opener against the visiting New York Knicks.

"But I think every day, every week, every month, I'll continue to get better and better. My body will continue to ramp up, and the play will get better."

James, who signed a two-year deal to join the Sixers this offseason, put up 20.9 points per game in his final campaign with the Los Angeles Lakers.

He has averaged 15.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, 6.8 assists and 1.8 steals in his first four appearances with the 76ers.

James is playing 33 minutes a game, but managed his workload by sitting out the first game of a back-to-back last week.

The Sixers would especially benefit from James increasing his production Friday considering the absence of Jaylen Brown, who was ruled out ahead of the game due to a left knee injury.

The Sixers will look for more production from James while Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope potentially increase their playing time in the short term.

articles.title: Chet Holmgren Injury Update, Latest News on Thunder Star's Status, Return Timeline Amid Knee Issue
articles.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder are losing two more starters in addition to Jalen Williams.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder are losing two more starters in addition to Jalen Williams.

Chet Holmgren will be sidelined for the next two months while Cason Wallace will be out for the near future, the Thunder announced Friday.

Holmgren underwent a "biological treatment" Friday on a patellar tendon tear in his right knee, the Thunder announced.

He is expected to return to play in eight to 10 weeks, according to the Thunder.

Wallace underwent left shoulder surgery and will be "re-evaluated prior to the end of the 2026-27 regular season," the team reported.

Wallace, Holmgren and Williams last played Oct. 25 against the Los Angeles Clippers.

Wallace suffered his shoulder injury in the game, in which Williams suffered a broken left fibula and dislocated left ankle .

The Thunder announced Thursday Williams had undergone surgery involving "reconstruction of ankle ligaments" and would also be evaluated prior to the end of the regular season.

Holmgren also felt "mild discomfort in his right knee" for the first time the day of the Clippers game, according to the Thunder.

This will mark the first extended absence from Holmgren since he suffered a pelvic fracture in November 2024. He returned later that spring to contribute to the Thunder's 2025 title run, then played 69 games of an All-Defensive campaign last season.

The Thunder will be eligible for a hardship roster exception given the injuries, which prefaced the franchise signing free agent guard Ochai Agbaji, per Spotrac's Keith Smith.

Smith noted the exception does not impact the Thunder's salary cap status, and Oklahoma City will likely want to remain beneath the second apron going forward. The franchise had $4.6 million in space beneath the second apron after signing Agbaji, per Smith.

Wallace had averaged 6.3 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 2.3 steals, while Williams put up 13.7 points and 4.7 rebounds per game prior to their respective injuries.

Holmgren had averaged 12 points, 9.3 rebounds and three blocks per game before his procedure.

The team will now need to evaluate how to replace that missing production and defense with only Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Isaiah Hartenstein remaining from Oklahoma City's season-opening starting lineup.

Alex Caruso has also been ruled out of Saturday's matchup at the Houston Rockets with a right ankle sprain. Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell and Kenrich Williams could continue to see elevated playing time as the Thunder look to build on their 4-1 start despite roster limitations.

articles.title: Thunder's Chet Holmgren will miss 8-10 weeks after undergoing treatment on patellar tendon tear
articles.summary: Holmgren underwent a successful 'biological treatment' on his right knee but will miss time while recovering, the team announced Friday.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder's injury issues continue as star center Chet Holmgren is set to miss significant time. The team announced Friday that Holmgren will be out eight to 10 weeks after undergoing treatment for a small patellar tendon tear in his right knee.

Per the team, Holmgren was assessed after experiencing "mild discomfort" in his knee last week. After consulting with specialists, Holmgren underwent "a biological treatment" in that knee, which the team said was "successful."

Holmgren did not play in the Thunder's past two matchups after being ruled out with right knee patellar tendinitis. Based on Oklahoma City's timeline, Holmgren will likely not return to the court until December or January.

In the same announcement, the Thunder said Cason Wallace successfully underwent surgery on a labral tear in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the season. Wallace sustained the tear earlier this week, just a week after the guard signed a five-year, $139 million extension .

Oklahoma City has suffered injury blow after injury blow early in the season, with several key players sidelined in the past week . Starting guard Jalen Williams went down on Sunday with a gruesome leg injury ; he underwent surgery this week to repair his fractured fibula and dislocated ankle, and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season. To make things worse, key bench player Alex Caruso sprained his ankle Monday and is likely to be out for several games.

Holmgren, Wallace and Williams all sustained their injuries on the same day, with Caruso's ankle injury coming a day later.

"We're not doing great," head coach Mark Daigneault said after Williams was carted off in Sunday's win. "That's tough on the guys."

The flurry of injuries will significantly test the Thunder's depth. Though Oklahoma City has Shai Gilgeous-Alexander to hold things down, it'll also be missing three starters and a top bench player. Jared McCain (who was traded to the Thunder last February), Ajay Mitchell and Kenrich Williams have been filling in as starters, with Mitchell dropping 29 points in Wednesday's loss to the Dallas Mavericks.

articles.title: LeBron Has Best Game with 76ers vs. Knicks, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Brunson, Top Players
articles.summary: Tyrese Maxey and LeBron James lifted the Philadelphia 76ers to a 98-93 win over the New York Knicks on Friday night, combining for 57 points to lead Philadelphia to a victory in its first NBA Cup game of the season.
articles.body:
Tyrese Maxey and LeBron James lifted the Philadelphia 76ers to a 98-93 win over the New York Knicks on Friday night, combining for 57 points to lead Philadelphia to a victory in its first NBA Cup game of the season.

The Knicks, who are the defending NBA and NBA Cup champions, entered Friday's game as 3.5-point underdogs against the 76ers, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , after opening the season with three consecutive losses and a 2-3 record.

The 76ers were without starting guard Jaylen Brown, who was sidelined with left patellar tendinopathy. Brown reported left knee soreness following Wednesday's 114-109 win over the Indiana Pacers, according to Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.

Despite being without Brown, who is averaging 20.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 4.2 assists per game, the 76ers pulled off the win to improve to 5-1 and maintain their near-perfect start to the season.

The Knicks have fallen to 2-4 in a shocking turnaround from just four months ago, when they were hoisting the Larry O'Brien Trophy after winning the NBA Finals.

Philadelphia 76ers: 1-0 (CUP), 5-1 (OVR)

Cleveland Cavaliers: First game Nov. 6 at 7:30 p.m. ET

Miami Heat: First game Oct. 30 at 8:00 p.m. ET

Indiana Pacers: First game Oct. 30 at 8:00 p.m. ET

Group Play: Oct. 30, Nov. 6, 13, 20, 24, 25 and 27

James finished with 20 points — his best performance in a 76ers jersey — nine rebounds and eight assists to help lead Philadelphia to an impressive win.

Maxey added 27 points, four rebounds and four assists after leading the team at halftime with 18 points on 8-of-12 shooting from the field.

Maxey has gotten off to a hot start this season, with his lowest-scoring game coming against the Milwaukee Bucks, when he finished with 26 points. He is averaging 28.4 points per game, which ranks fourth in the league.

Joel Embiid finished with 10 points, seven rebounds and seven assists while VJ Edgecombe added 13 points. Anfernee Simons exploded off the bench for 21 points.

For the Knicks, Brunson led the way with 24 points, five rebounds and six assists, continuing his strong play after his 38-point performance on Wednesday.

Karl-Anthony Towns added 22 points and 12 rebounds to record a double-double, finishing strong with a fourth-quarter surge.

The Knicks had a balanced scoring effort in the first half, with four starters recording seven points, while Towns led the way with nine.

OG Anunoby finished with nine points, while Mikal Bridges added 12 points. Miles McBride contributed 10 points off the bench.

Philadelphia opened the game with a 29-21 lead after the first quarter before extending its advantage to 14 points. The Knicks then went on a run to cut the deficit to nine heading into halftime, with the 76ers leading 53-44.

Brunson exploded for 13 points in the third quarter to help the Knicks stay within reach, as both teams scored 24 points in the period. Simons stepped up for the 76ers in the third, helping Philadelphia maintain its lead at 77-68 headed into the final quarter.

Both teams put on a show down the stretch. The Knicks took the lead by one with 1:32 remaining, the 76ers closed out the home win with a 9-3 run, including a 5-0 spurt to seal the victory.

New York will host the Brooklyn Nets on Monday at 7:30 p.m. ET, while the 76ers will hit the road to face the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday at 6 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Jalen Brunson Jokes Josh Hart is 'Old as S--t' After Knicks Star's Comments About Fatigue
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson apparently isn't surprised to hear his teammate Josh Hart is talking about tiredness six games into the defense of their 2026 NBA title.
articles.body:
New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson apparently isn't surprised to hear his teammate Josh Hart is talking about tiredness six games into the defense of their 2026 NBA title.

"Josh said he feels the fatigue? Well, Josh is old as s--t, so," Brunson joked to reporters after opening NBA Cup play with a 98-93 Friday night loss at the Philadelphia 76ers.

Brunson was referencing a postgame interview in which Hart said the Knicks "all feel the fatigue" after playing last season until mid-June.

"We've got to fight through it," said Hart, who acknowledged ahead of the season he is playing with a finger injury he cannot surgically repair until he retires.

"Six games in, but we've got to find a way to make sure we get our bodies ready to play every day. I think mentally we're there, we've just got to find it physically."

The Knicks fell to 2-4 with the Friday night loss to the Sixers, which have now beaten the defending champions twice this season.

New York will look to start turning things around starting with a Monday game against the winless Brooklyn Nets to avoid falling further down the Eastern Conference standings.

articles.title: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry put $25 million behind a mission that could change 10,000 Oakland children's lives
articles.summary: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have committed $25 million over five years to give about 10,000 Oakland elementary students one-on-one reading tutoring.
articles.body: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have committed $25 million over five years to give about 10,000 Oakland elementary students one-on-one reading tutoring. Their Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation announced the plan on Aug. 29, 2024, and it is the largest literacy investment the foundation has made. The program targets Oakland Unified School District students who read two or more grade levels behind. The need is wide. Nearly half of the district’s elementary students are performing below grade level. Workday, a longtime partner, has also given more than $11 million to the foundation.How will the Currys’ $25 million help 10,000 Oakland kids learn to read?Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry launched Eat. Learn. Play. in 2019 to focus on nutrition, education and physical activity. This commitment falls under education. Students will get high-dosage tutoring built to strengthen their reading and writing, the kind of help many families cannot afford on their own.The foundation has early proof to point to. A spring pilot ran at 18 Oakland elementary schools and reached nearly 600 students. Preliminary results from one tracking group show 85% of students closed their foundational skills gaps.Oakland Unified is adding $25 million of its own for small-group tutoring. The district aims to serve up to 4,500 students a year by 2029.What else has Eat. Learn. Play. done for Oakland students?Curry has put his name behind the foundation since 2019, and the totals are big. Over seven years, it has invested more than $100 million in Oakland kids, delivered 35 million meals, remodeled 25 schoolyards and six gymnasiums, and redesigned 14 cafeterias. More than 1 million new books have reached OUSD students.For the four-time champion, learning has a clear target: every Oakland elementary student reading proficiently by the end of third grade. The foundation says its high-impact tutoring now reaches more than 10,000 OUSD students.July brought two honors. The Hollywood Reporter named the Currys Philanthropists of the Year, and Curry received the Muhammad Ali Sports Humanitarian Award.Books go home with kids, too. Last December’s book fairs ran at 47 OUSD schools, where more than 17,000 students could each choose four new books to take home. The plan called for more than 68,000 books in all.Fundraising comes from several directions. An April sneaker auction of more than 70 pairs worn by Curry raised $1.7 million, and the Workday Charity Classic added $5.6 million, helped by a matching gift from Workday CEO Aneel Bhusri.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dillon Brooks Ejected for Kicking Jamal Murray in Groin During Suns vs. Nuggets NBA Cup Game
articles.summary: The Phoenix Suns' Dillon Brooks was ejected from Friday night's NBA Cup opener against the Denver Nuggets due to what officials ruled was an "unnecessary and excessive" kick to Jamal Murray's groin.
articles.body:
The Phoenix Suns' Dillon Brooks was ejected from Friday night's NBA Cup opener against the Denver Nuggets due to what officials ruled was an "unnecessary and excessive" kick to Jamal Murray's groin.

Brooks made contact with Murray while rising up for a jump shot with 8:05 left in the third quarter. He was assessed a Flagrant 2 foul on the play.

Brooks was called for an offensive foul before officials reviewed the play and upgraded the penalty. Murray, who fell to the ground after the initial contact, remained in the game.

Brooks had recorded 22 points in 21 minutes on the court prior to his exit. The Suns were trailing 84-76 at the time.

He had put up 20 points in the first half alone, and by the time of his ejection had shot 9-for-12 from the field and 4-for-6 from deep while leading the Suns in scoring.

The Suns were heading into Saturday's matchup with a 1-2 record and rumors of discontent in the locker room.

NBA insider Chris Haynes recently reported he feels there is "frustration" among Suns players over the team's decision to aim for offensive distribution by committee rather than relying on a traditional point guard.

Brooks has averaged 14.7 points across those first three contests while adding 3.7 rebounds, 4.4 assists and one steal per game.

Saturday's matchup marked the opening of NBA Cup play for the Suns, which are competing in West Group A alongside the Nuggets, Dallas Mavericks, Houston Rockets, Phoenix Suns and Utah Jazz. The Suns will resume in-season tournament play Nov. 20 in Salt Lake City.

articles.title: LeBron James Discusses His Longevity, Being Calming Presence for 76ers Amid 5-1 Start to Season
articles.summary: LeBron James says he thinks his unprecedented longevity in the NBA has allowed him to be a "calming factor" late in games for the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
LeBron James says he thinks his unprecedented longevity in the NBA has allowed him to be a "calming factor" late in games for the Philadelphia 76ers.

James spoke about his mindset shortly after scoring 20 points as the Sixers opened NBA Cup play with a Friday night win over the visiting New York Knicks.

"I didn't think I would still be playing in year 24, that's for sure, but I knew I would have a lasting career, because I know how much I put into my body and my mind, and training, and things of that nature, every single year, every single offseason," James told reporters Friday (h/t Chris Hine of the Philadelphia Inquirer.

James continued, "I guess the best teacher in life is experience. I've been in really big games... For me to be able to be a calming factor for our team, late game, it's just an experience that I have.

"If it's me with the ball, without the ball, being able to just put guys in the right position, just trying to talk them through it... It's something I want to continue to pour into the team."

Jalen Brunson helped the Knicks pull ahead by one point with one and half minutes remaining of Saturday night's matchup in Philadelphia.

James responded with an answering jump shot to regain a lead the Sixers held until the final buzzer.

The 76ers improved to 5-1 with Friday night's win to tie the Detroit Pistons for the best record in the Eastern Conference.

The Sixers will now prepare for a quick turnaround before a Saturday evening game at the Charlotte Hornets. James and Joel Embiid could be sitting out as part of their load management strategy involving back-to-backs, while Jaylen Brown's status will remain in question after he was ruled out of Friday's game with a knee injury.

articles.title: Steph Curry Passes Dominique Wilkins on NBA All-Time Scoring List, Where Does He Rank Among Greats?
articles.summary: Stephen Curry continued to climb up the NBA's all-time scoring list during the Golden State Warriors' clash with the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday night.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry continued to climb up the NBA's all-time scoring list during the Golden State Warriors' clash with the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday night.

Curry scored the 26,669th point of his career during the contest, passing Hall of Famer Dominique Wilkins for the No. 18 spot on the league's all-time scoring leaderboard.

Curry is now ahead of Wilkins, Tim Duncan, Paul Pierce, John Havlicek and Kevin Garnett on the list. He's also nearing Oscar Robertson and his 26,710 career points at the No. 17 spot on the leaderboard.

DeMar DeRozan sits at No. 16 with 26,763 points, although DeRozan's overall scoring total will continue to rise as he begins his first season as a member of the Denver Nuggets.

Curry's status among the top 20 scorers in NBA history is particularly impressive considering the time he's missed due to injuries throughout his career, including a 2019-20 campaign in which he was limited to just five games played.

This season, he entered Friday's action averaging 28.8 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.5 steals per game while shooting 47.7 percent from the field and 38.9 percent from three-point territory.

articles.title: NBA Cup 2026: Defending champ Knicks fall to Sixers, again, in first night of play
articles.summary: It was no Jaylen Brown, no problem for the Sixers against the defending champs.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks opened their NBA title defense with a loss to the Philadelphia 76ers . They began their NBA Cup title defense the same way on Friday.

The first night of 2026 NBA Cup play saw the defending champions once again fall to Philadelphia, this time by a score of 98-93. The Sixers ultimately prevailed despite the absence of Jaylen Brown due to patellar tendinopathy .

New York nearly pulled off a double-digit comeback in the fourth quarter, taking the lead at one point. However, the Sixers immediately responded with five straight points, capped off by a 3-pointer from VJ Edgecombe.

Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers with 27 points on 10-of-19 shooting, while James wasn't far from a triple-double with 20 points, 9 rebounds and 8 assists. Anfernee Simons added 21 points on 11 shots off the bench.

Beyond the NBA Cup, the loss continues a rough start for New York, whose overall record is now 2-4. And now they're 0-1 in Cup play, in a group that also includes the Cleveland Cavaliers, Miami Heat and Indiana Pacers.

The Knicks also lost their NBA Cup opener last season, but won the next three games to earn first place in their group. They defeated the San Antonio Spurs in the championship game, then went on to win their first NBA Finals in 53 years.

The Los Angeles Lakers began their game against the Golden State Warriors on a 40-15 run, with Luka Dončić clearly trying to make an example of Yaxel Lendeborg after their previous run in . When the Lakers star subbed out to begin the second quarter, he was already at 25 points, 5 assists, 3 rebounds and 2 steals.

And then the Warriors outscored the Lakers by 42 for the rest of the game, which ended as a 112-95 Golden State win. As for Dončić, well, let's just say Stephen Curry had a response for him.

One of the closest finishes of the night was between the Dallas Mavericks and Houston Rockets, with Cooper Flagg delivering the dagger after trailing for much of the second half.

That game-sealing shot was part of a 33-point, 9-rebound, 6-assists night for Flagg, who turns 20 on Dec. 21. With that statline, he joins Luka Dončić as the only teenagers in NBA history to record three straight 25-5-5 games . That's a bittersweet stat for Mavericks fans.

Kyrie Irving actually led Dallas in scoring, posting 35 points on 12-of-19 shooting.

Does this kick below the belt constitute both unnecessary and excessive contact? The officials decided it did, hitting Phoenix Suns star Dillon Brooks with a flagrant 2 foul for a kick to Jamal Murray's groin.

The Suns broadcast… disagreed with the decision .

That decision wound up being rather important, as the Denver Nuggets went on to win 127-120 behind a 39-point game from Murray. Brooks exited with 22 points on 9-of-12 shooting.

AJ Dybantsa has looked plenty comfortable early in his NBA career. So have the Washington Wizards for that matter.

The Wizards blew out the Charlotte Hornets 95-79, with their new big 3 all filling out the stat sheet. Dybantsa, the No. 1 overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, had 17 points on 11 shots and 7 rebounds in his home debut, while Anthony Davis led all scorers with 25 points and 13 rebounds.

Trae Young added 21 points, 9 assists, 6 rebounds and 3 assists.

More notable was the Wizards' team defense, which held Charlotte to 29.7% shooting from the floor. It was the first time Washington held a team to below 80 points since March 9, 2015 .

articles.title: Steph Sparks Warriors Comeback vs. Lakers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Luka, Reaves, Top Players
articles.summary: Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors stormed back from a 25-point deficit to defeat Luka Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers 112-95 on Friday, behind 31 points from Curry.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors stormed back from a 25-point deficit to defeat Luka Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers 112-95 on Friday, behind 31 points from Curry.

The Lakers were 2.5-point favorites over the Warriors at home heading into their opening NBA Cup matchup, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but collapsed after building an early lead.

The win marked Golden State's first victory over Los Angeles this season after the Warriors lost the season opener 127-105, despite 23 points from Curry.

With a three-game winning streak, Golden State improved to 3-3, while the Lakers dropped their second game of the season to fall to 4-2.

Golden State Warriors: 1-0 (CUP), 3-3 (OVR)

Los Angeles Lakers: 0-1 (CUP), 4-2 (OVR)

Portland Trail Blazers: First game Nov. 6 at 10:00 p.m. ET

San Antonio Spurs: First game Nov. 6 at 10:00 p.m. ET

Sacramento Kings: First game Nov. 6 at 10:00 p.m. ET

Group Play: Oct. 30, Nov. 6, 13, 20, 24, 25 and 27

Curry led the Warriors with 31 points, going 8-of-14 from deep, continuing his strong start to the season. He is averaging 28.8 points per game, which ranks third in the league in his 17th NBA season.

The veteran is coming off a 44-point performance against the Minnesota Timberwolves, adding eight rebounds, six assists and two steals.

Brandin Podziemski added 21 points and six assists while Georges Niang contributed 11 points and De'Anthony Melton added 16 points off the bench. Draymond facilitated with nine assists, three steals and a block.

Doncic finished with 37 points, adding seven rebounds and five assists to lead the Lakers. He has gotten off to an electric start this season, averaging 36 points per game to lead the league after scoring 41 and 52 points in his previous two games.

Austin Reaves added 21 points, while Jake LaRavia, Matisse Thybulle and Walker Kessler contributed 10 points each.

The first half was a game of runs, with both teams finding their rhythm and putting together scoring spurts.

After the Lakers opened the game with a 14-0 run and later added a 12-0 spurt in the first quarter, the Warriors responded with an 18-0 run of their own, followed by a 16-2 run in the second quarter to erase the deficit and tie the game at 53 heading into halftime.

Curry led the Warriors with 14 points at the break, going 4-of-7 from 3-point range, while De'Anthony Melton added 13 points.

The Lakers were led by Doncic with 24 points, four rebounds and five assists, while Austin Reaves added 10 points.

Golden State battled back to take its first lead since going up 2-0 in the third quarter, carrying a five-point advantage into the fourth.

The Warriors continued their momentum with another run, carrying an 18-0 spurt into the fourth quarter to build a 96-80 lead with just over eight minutes remaining and set themselves up for the home win.

The Lakers will host the Toronto Raptors on Sunday at 9 p.m. ET, while the Warriors will host the Los Angeles Clippers at 8:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Kobe Bryant’s high school jersey sells at auction for record-breaking $2.2 million
articles.summary: kobeEverything started at Lower Merion High School for Kobe Bryant. On Friday, Sotheby’s reported that one of Bryant’s game-worn No.33 jerseys sold for a rec...
articles.body:
On Friday, Sotheby's reported that one of Bryant's game-worn No.33 jerseys sold for a record-breaking $2.2 million, making it the most expensive high school jersey ever sold at an auction.

"This Lower Merion jersey is where Kobe's story starts, before the rings, the records, and the Mamba Mentality, when he was just a kid in a gym outworking everyone. This jersey symbolizes that greatness has a beginning, and this jersey was there for it," reads the description from Sotheby's.

This is not the first time the jersey has been moved, as it was sold in 2013 for $51,400.

The report of the jersey read that the item had 26 bids, with seven different bidders competing for the highly sought-after item.

Bryant's jersey sale eclipsed LeBron James' St. Vincent-St. Mary jersey, which was worn during his infamous 2002 Sports Illustrated "The Chosen One" cover and sold in 2024 for $1.3 million.

Sotheby's reported that Bryant wore the sold jersey during his junior season, in a March 1995 matchup against Hazleton, Pa., Area.

The jersey goes into the long list of highly coveted memorabilia from Bryant. The most expensive piece was a 2007-2008 dual-autograph card from Upper Deck that features Bryant and Michael Jordan, which sold for $12.6 million in August 2022.

Bryant's Lower Merion jersey is the only basketball uniform he's worn that didn't have the words "Lakers" or "Los Angeles" across the chest, as he entered the NBA draft immediately after finishing high school.

Bryant spent the entirety of his 20-year career with Los Angeles and is regarded as not only one of the greatest Lakers ever, but one of the best basketball players of all time.

His career finished with him having five NBA titles, two Finals MVPs, one-time league MVP, and an 18-time All-Star selection.

In 2017, the Lakers retired both Bryant's No. 8 and No. 24 jersey numbers , making him the only player in the NBA to have two numbers retired by a team.

A year after he tragically died in 2020, he was inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame .

articles.title: Mavericks’ Kyrie Irving earns MVP chants during season-high performance vs. Rockets
articles.summary: The Dallas Mavericks’ dynamic duo of Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg got to work as they helped bring down the Houston Rockets in the NBA Cup, 116-111. It was...
articles.body:
The Dallas Mavericks ' dynamic duo of Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg got to work as they helped bring down the Houston Rockets in the NBA Cup, 116-111. It was the Rockets' first loss of the season.

Irving had a game-high 35 points with four rebounds and nine assists, including some key free throws to ice the game. During one of his trips to the line with seconds left in the game, the Dallas crowd serenaded him with MVP chants to show appreciation for his game-winning performance.

Not to be outdone, Cooper Flagg had 33 points, nine rebounds and six assists. The second-year player is showing no ill-effects of the left shoulder injury that he suffered last week against the Indiana Pacers . He has now topped 26 points in each of his last three games. With the win over the Rockets, the Mavs have now won three games in a row.

Irving is still working his way back from the knee injury that sidelined him last season . It's highly unlikely that he can compete for MVP this season, but his game against the Rockets shows that he still has MVP-caliber performances left in him.

Moreover, Irving has Flagg to carry the heavy load for the Mavs during the regular season. That can allow the 34-year-old Irving to conserve his body and push only during bigger games, like the NBA Cup contest against the rival Rockets. And if the Mavs are able to break into playoff contention in the competitive West, Irving can potentially do some damage come playoff time.
